```{python}
import gzip
import json
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display
source = Path('inputs/source')
ledger = json.loads((source / 'source-ledger.json').read_text())
run = json.loads(gzip.decompress(Path('results/native-results.json.gz').read_bytes()))
data = pd.read_csv('results/comparisons.csv', float_precision='round_trip')
prior = json.loads((source / 'issue-730-shared-row.json').read_text())['quantity']
current = json.loads(Path('results/shared-row-reference.json').read_text())['quantity']
refs = pd.read_csv(source / 'esteso-1989-reference-coefficients.csv')
shared = data[(data.ethanol_mass_percent == 60) & (data.molality_mol_kg == .5)].iloc[0]
counts = data.groupby('ethanol_mass_percent').agg(
    rows=('row_id','size'), reproduced=('outcome', lambda s: (s == 'reproduced').sum()),
    numerical_resolved=('numerical_resolution', lambda s: (s == 'resolved').sum()),
    density_trace_converged=('activity_density_trace_qualified','sum'))
summary = data.groupby('ethanol_mass_percent').agg(
    m_min=('molality_mol_kg','min'), m_max=('molality_mol_kg','max'),
    error_min=('signed_error','min'), error_max=('signed_error','max'),
    absolute_error_max=('absolute_error','max'), relative_error_min=('relative_error','min'),
    relative_error_max=('relative_error','max'), AARD_percent=('relative_error',lambda s: 100*s.abs().mean()))
passed = data[data.outcome == 'reproduced']
density = [s['convergence'] for a in run['activities'] for s in a['trace']['spans'] if s['name'] == 'solve_density']
```

## Result and meaning

The native Figiel prediction agrees with `{python} str(len(passed))` of
`{python} str(len(data))` Table I coefficients at the fixed printed-precision
criterion. The other `{python} str((data.outcome == 'not reproduced').sum())`
rows are **converged disagreements, cause undetermined**. This is a physical
comparison with activities inferred from cell voltages and fitted reference
coefficients, with separate numerical verification of the calculations.
It does not establish independent physical validation: Figiel cites Esteso,
and independence from parameter-development evidence has not been established.

The calculation uses `{python} str(run['temperature_K'])` K and
`{python} str(run['pressure_Pa'])` Pa, with formula-unit molality per kilogram
of salt-free mixed solvent. Pressure is a declared calculation condition;
Esteso's experimental pressure is unreported. Solvent-only mole fractions
come from `inputs/solvent-compositions.csv`, using the selected packet's NIST
molar masses. The component order, stoichiometry, solvent fractions and both
variants are retained in the native result and its reference records.

## All solvent series

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(12, 7), layout='constrained')
for ax, (percent, group) in zip(axes.flat, data.groupby('ethanol_mass_percent')):
    ax.scatter(group.molality_mol_kg, group.gamma_pm_m, marker='o', facecolors='none', edgecolors='#0072B2', label='Esteso Table I')
    ax.scatter(group.molality_mol_kg, group.predicted_gamma, marker='x', color='#D55E00', label='Native Figiel')
    ax.set(xscale='log', xlabel='NaCl molality / (mol kg⁻¹ mixed solvent)', ylabel='Mean ionic coefficient γ± / 1', title=f'{percent} mass % ethanol')
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', which='minor', labelbottom=False)
    if percent == 90:
        ax.set_xticks([.004, .01, .04], labels=['0.004', '0.01', '0.04'])
    ax.grid(alpha=.2)
axes.flat[0].legend()
plt.show()
display(HTML(counts.to_html()))
display(HTML(summary.to_html(float_format=lambda x: f'{x:.8g}')))
```

The figure shows discrete predictions at the observation coordinates; it
contains no fitted or interpolated curve. The logarithmic molality axis
resolves the dilute rows. The tables give row counts, numerical resolution,
and signed, absolute and relative errors by solvent. Average absolute relative
deviation (AARD) is the arithmetic mean of absolute signed relative errors,
multiplied by a percentage factor, over every row in the corresponding solvent;
the row count is its denominator. No incomplete-grid average is used.

The only agreeing row is shown below. Agreement of that row does not make its
solvent series a reproduction at printed precision.

```{python}
display(HTML(passed[['ethanol_mass_percent','molality_mol_kg','gamma_pm_m','predicted_gamma','absolute_error']].to_html(index=False, float_format=lambda x: f'{x:.16g}')))
total = dict(rows=len(data), unavailable=data.predicted_gamma.isna().sum(),
             signed_error_min=data.signed_error.min(), signed_error_max=data.signed_error.max(),
             relative_error_min=data.relative_error.min(), relative_error_max=data.relative_error.max(),
             AARD_percent=100*data.relative_error.abs().mean())
display(HTML(pd.DataFrame([total]).to_html(index=False, float_format=lambda x: f'{x:.8g}')))
```

## Fixed numerical criteria and actual density evidence

The printed-precision criterion is absolute error at most
`{python} str(run['criteria']['printed_absolute'])`. The independent numerical
allocation is `{python} str(run['criteria']['numerical_absolute'])` in the
coefficient. Neither is experimental uncertainty. Effective stopping settings
are retained on each reference and activity record. The baseline uses native
defaults; the refined declaration changes only association and density residual
criteria, leaving all physical inputs, the analytic infinite-dilution reference
and fixed work limits unchanged. The native reference uses ion insertion at the
ion-free solvent state, as specified by [ALG-REFERENCE](../../../engine/docs/science/algorithms.md#alg-reference).
Its terminal molality is zero; no dilution ladder or terminal-change estimate exists.

```{python}
reference_rows = [dict(variant=r['variant'], ethanol_mass_percent=r['ethanol_mass_percent'],
    terminal_molality_mol_kg=r['molality'], reference_log_change=r['convergence_error'],
    association_residual=next(x['value'] for x in r['solver_options'] if x['name']=='ASSOCIATION_RESIDUAL'),
    density_residual=next(x['value'] for x in r['solver_options'] if x['name']=='DENSITY_ROOT_RESIDUAL'))
    for r in run['references']]
display(HTML(pd.DataFrame(reference_rows).fillna('unavailable').to_html(index=False)))
```

The largest baseline–refined coefficient difference is
`{python} f"{data.refinement_difference.max():.8g}"`.
The terminal-change estimate is **unavailable**, rather than zero, for both
analytic-reference variants. Numerical resolution uses the unchanged
`{python} str(run['criteria']['numerical_absolute'])` allocation and requires
the baseline–refined difference to lie within it. A comparison lying within
that allocation of the printed boundary would be unresolved; there are
`{python} str((data.outcome == 'unresolved').sum())` here. Density and association
diagnostics and the refinement comparison supply numerical verification;
the allocation is not a rigorous total error bound.

Each actual activity call has its own captured native density solve. Across
both variants, `{python} str(len(density))` captured density convergence records
have a maximum residual/criterion ratio of
`{python} f"{max(c['residual']/c['criterion']['value'] for c in density):.8g}"`.
The trace includes span parentage, selected-root events, root counts,
association convergence and analytic infinite-dilution reference spans. The trace-incompleteness
count is `{python} str(sum(a['trace']['incomplete'] for a in run['activities']) + sum(r['trace']['incomplete'] for r in run['references']))`.
The activity binding omits its consumed State. Accordingly, density qualification
here means the actual captured solve's convergence evidence; no second solve
was substituted, and no full exposed-state or global-stability claim is made.

## Shared row and interpretation of disagreement

The current shared-row coefficient is `{python} repr(float(shared.predicted_gamma))`;
its Table I target is `{python} str(shared.gamma_pm_m)`. It equals the accepted
analytic-reference value in [the current reference record](results/shared-row-reference.json),
whose log value is `{python} repr(current['log_value'])` and terminal molality is
`{python} repr(current['reference']['molality'])` mol/kg. That record retains the
actual native-source, extension and parameter-packet hashes and execution identity.
It supplies no terminal-change estimate.

The historical #730 coefficient is `{python} repr(prior['value'])`, with run
`{python} prior['execution_identity']['run_id']` and its original source hash,
Engine identity and terminal reference unchanged in
[issue-730-shared-row.json](inputs/source/issue-730-shared-row.json).
Exact equality with that historical value is
`{python} str(float(shared.predicted_gamma) == prior['value'])`; the current minus
historical difference is `{python} f"{float(shared.predicted_gamma)-prior['value']:.16g}"`.
[#823](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/823) replaced the dilution
ladder with the analytic reference. This small change is below both fixed
criteria and does not explain the physical disagreement.

The retained pre-#823 run had one reproduced and 122 not-reproduced rows.
On main before this record correction, the stale requirement for two ladder
estimates classified all 123 rows as unresolved and the historical-equality
self-check stopped. The refreshed comparison has
`{python} str((data.outcome == 'reproduced').sum())` reproduced,
`{python} str((data.outcome == 'not reproduced').sum())` not reproduced, and
`{python} str((data.outcome == 'unresolved').sum())` unresolved rows.
The numerical allocation and printed-precision criterion are unchanged.

The salt-free composition, mixed-solvent mass basis, charge-neutral
stoichiometry, parameter family and pressure match the accepted declarations.
The tightened solve changes are far smaller than the discrepancies. This rules
out the tested tolerance sensitivity as their explanation. The
[#730 comparison](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/blob/759c95d80c25557c176d21ca895ba5e3b288dc3b/analyses/reproduction/2026-eos-literature-handoff/notebook.qmd) found that the
accepted change in cross-solvent association does not explain the shared-row
miss. The [#726 aqueous comparison](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/blob/759c95d80c25557c176d21ca895ba5e3b288dc3b/analyses/reproduction/2020-haslam/notebook.qmd) also found
limited agreement, with allocation among model terms, fitting and source
selection unresolved. Its pressure differs and it supplies no diagnosis of a
mixed-solvent mechanism.

The ethanol-rich series consistently overpredict Table I, whereas the water-rich series contain errors of both signs. The maximum absolute error and average absolute relative deviation are generally larger in the ethanol-rich series, but the trend is not monotonic and the molality grids differ. Disagreement also occurs at dilute points in the most water-rich series, so concentration extrapolation is not established as its cause.

Figiel, Yu and Held, in “Properties in Organic and Mixed Solvents” and Figure 9, present mixed-solvent predictions without additional fitting and compare NaCl in water–ethanol directly with Esteso. They report good mixed-solvent agreement, particularly at low concentration. This is a qualitative model-adequacy statement, not a printed-precision guarantee. The present comparison does not retain matching-state values of their plotted model curves. Their high-concentration NaBr caveat does not establish a cause for these NaCl deviations. The remaining difference has not been isolated to a model term, fitted parameter, source treatment or implementation difference; its cause remains undetermined. Neither the aqueous comparison nor the present solvent pattern establishes missing neutral pairing as the cause.

Source locator: [Figiel, Yu and Held (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.5c00475),
“Properties in Organic and Mixed Solvents,” discussion preceding Figure 9 and
Figure 9 caption, Esteso reference 85.

No numerical refusal occurred in either variant, so no failure retry or Engine
correction was warranted.

## Source quantities, uncertainty and exclusions

[Esteso et al. (1989)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00652989), Table I, printed
pp.280–281, supplies the activity targets and measured voltage differences.
The source ledger records the local PDF identity, table/page locators,
source-model equations and historical provenance. `source-verification.json`
retains the transcription checks and spot checks. The legacy observations
remain as historical input; superseded comparison figures and values are
identified by their exact Git record, with no retained producer attributed to them.

The source inconsistency is preserved: the Table I reference row gives
`{python} str(ledger['source_inconsistency']['table_I_gamma'])`, while section
3.4 gives `{python} str(ledger['source_inconsistency']['section_3_4_gamma'])`.
The literal Table I value remains the target; neither statement is recalibrated.
The fitted reference uncertainty is ±`{python} str(refs.gamma_pm_reference_uncertainty.iloc[0])`,
shared within a solvent series. Instrument resolution is
±`{python} str(refs.emf_resolution_mV.iloc[0])` mV and temperature control is
±`{python} str(refs.temperature_uncertainty_K.iloc[0])` K. Pointwise activity
covariance, solvent-weighing uncertainty and pressure uncertainty are unknown.
The misses therefore do not establish individual statistical significance.

Tables II–V and reference coefficients are recorded only. Table II contains
solvent reference properties used in the source data reduction, partly from
previous literature. Tables III–V contain fits of the source's extended
Debye–Hückel, Pitzer and neutral-pair models. Their fitted coefficients and
voltage residuals are not ePC-SAFT prediction targets. The selected Figiel
family has no neutral NaCl species. Source solvent association does not
supply that chemistry. Cell voltage is retained as the source observable;
no forward-voltage projection is computed. These are scope limitations and
require no Engine issue for the present activity comparison.

```{python}
for name, role in ledger['source_roles'].items():
    filename = f'esteso-1989-table-{name}.csv' if name != 'reference-coefficients' else 'esteso-1989-reference-coefficients.csv'
    if name != 'I':
        display(Markdown(f'### Source {name}: recorded only\n\n{role}'))
        display(HTML(pd.read_csv(source / filename, keep_default_na=False).to_html(index=False)))
```

[Figiel, Yu and Held (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.5c00475),
Tables 1–5 and Eqs.11–12, supplies the selected packet and its dielectric model.
Esteso's Table II permittivity is not substituted for that model, and no
parameter is refitted. The source equations and parameter packet retain their
own scientific owners; Python only submits declarations and reads native values.
